title: Fruits
summary: Discover 125 fruits, from familiar favorites to rare regional treasures, through size, weight, flavor, growing regions and surprising facts.
dataNote: Whole-fruit examples in grams, including natural peel, shell and seeds unless noted. A source may report a range, cultivar or sample mean. Chosen examples are not species averages or record comparisons. Undocumented weights are null and excluded from arithmetic. Burrow editorial ratings from 1 to 10, interpreting descriptions of ripe fruit: 1 barely sweet/tart, 5 moderate, 10 very sweet/tart. Not Brix, sugar grams, laboratory acidity, health scores or tastiness judgments. Breadfruit is rated at the mature cooking stage, plantain ripe and cooked, and olive after curing; weights remain whole fruits before cooking or curing. Cultivar, ripeness and personal perception change flavor. Burrow editorial findability bands, 1 to 5, for fresh fruit beyond its home region: 1 local harvest/specialist growers; 2 mostly regional/seasonal; 3 specialty markets; 4 regional staple traded abroad; 5 widely traded. Not a country count, current store inventory, conservation status or price. Based on described cultivation and trade, with no implied worldwide census. Origin or cultural/cultivation association, not an exhaustive distribution. Map pins mark representative places within the stated region, not a precisely known birthplace. Ancient origins and some species boundaries remain debated. Individually credited Commons photos. Stored as resized JPEGs for offline play; no botanical drawings or generated substitutes. Fruit cards include distinct species and familiar market types or cultivar groups, such as nectarines, satsumas and golden kiwifruit; the card count is not a count of unique species. Approximate longest dimension of one whole fruit body in centimetres: length for elongated fruit, diameter for round or flattened fruit. Excludes stems, leaves, crowns and projecting hairs or spines. Coconut includes its outer husk; cape gooseberry excludes its papery husk; cashew apple excludes the attached nut. Rounded examples are editorial selections within documented dimensions or named cultivar measurements, not species averages, maximum-size rankings or measurements of the pictured specimens. Source ranges and cultivar scope remain in each profile. Size and weight examples may come from different specimens. Collection order uses size, with alphabetical ties; weight-based games continue to use documented weights.

audience.readingLevel: short fruit facts with scientific names in the field notes

stats.label: Example weight
stats.note: Rounded from a measured whole-fruit sample mean of 156.2 g in the UK fruit and vegetable sampling report (2013). This is one survey sample, not a universal average.

stats.label: Example size
stats.note: Approximate longest fruit-body dimension, not a species average or a measurement of this photo. Reference diameter range: 2.5–12 cm. A rounded apple example selected within the broad cultivar range, rather than an average for every apple.

details.label: Size guide
details.value: Approximate longest dimension of one whole fruit body in centimetres: length for elongated fruit, diameter for round or flattened fruit. Excludes stems, leaves, crowns and projecting hairs or spines. Coconut includes its outer husk; cape gooseberry excludes its papery husk; cashew apple excludes the attached nut. Rounded examples are editorial selections within documented dimensions or named cultivar measurements, not species averages, maximum-size rankings or measurements of the pictured specimens. Source ranges and cultivar scope remain in each profile. Size and weight examples may come from different specimens. Collection order uses size, with alphabetical ties; weight-based games continue to use documented weights.

details.label: Comparison guide
details.value: Sizes and weights are examples, not fixed species averages, and may describe different specimens. Sweetness and tartness are game ratings, not sugar content or tastiness scores. Availability uses broad bands, not country counts.

details.label: Map note
details.value: Origin or cultural/cultivation association, not an exhaustive distribution. Map pins mark representative places within the stated region, not a precisely known birthplace. Ancient origins and some species boundaries remain debated.
